children: Saloni Shukla Mumbai: Indian banks have financed about a dozen M&A deals involving more than 10,000 crore in acquisition funding after the central bank eased takeover-financing rules effective July 1, people familiar with the matter told ET. Bankers said demand is picking up across sectors, with lenders financing up to 75% of the deal value.

State Bank of India (SBI), the country's largest mass lender and the biggest government entity by market value, has emerged as one of the most active participants, with nearly a dozen transactions either completed or in various stages of execution, said the people cited above. Other domestic lenders, including HDFC Bank, Kotak Mahindra Bank, ICICI Bank, Axis Bank and RBL Bank, have also participated in acquisition-financing transactions in recent months, alongside foreign lenders such as HSBC, Citibank, MUFG and Barclays, sources said. The emerging business represents a significant lending opportunity for Indian banks.

title: Domestic Banks Step Up to Fund India Deal Boom
